To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cardiac Cl- conductances activated by cAMP-dependent phosphorylation are regulated by both protein kinase-dependent and protein phosphatase-dependent dephosphorylations, and that these processes are functionally distinct.

the cardiac Cl- conductances activated by cAMP-dependent phosphorylation are functionally heterogeneous and can be distinguished by the different contributions of their phospho-forms to whole-cell conductance.
the Cl- conductance regulated by PKA and protein phosphatases in mammalian heart is composed of two functionally distinct phosphoforms that differ with respect to their relative stabilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the control of the cardiac Cl- channel.
the molecular basis for regulation of cardiac Cl(-) conductance by protein phosphorylation.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of Cl- channels in the heart.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are two distinct phosphoproteins that underlie activation and deactivation of the protein kinase-regulated cardiac Cl conductance.
the PKA-regulation of cardiac Cl- channels involves two distinct phosphorylation sites.
the Cl- channel is phosphorylated at two sites by PKA and that the two phosphorylated states of the channel are functionally distinct.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PKA phosphorylates a protein, which in turn activates a Cl- conductive pathway, and that this protein can be phosphorylated at two different sites, one of which is more susceptible to dephosphorylaton by type 1 and 3 phosphatases.

the PKA-activated Cl- conductance is composed of two functionally distinct forms of the Cl- channel, each phosphorylated at a different site, with the first form having a much higher rate constant for dephosphorylating than the second.

PKA phosphorylates the cardiac Cl- channel, that phosphorylation results in a conductance that is sensitive to protein phosphatases of type 1 and 10A, and that dephosphorylated Cl- channels are not available for rephosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the PKA-regulatory mechanism for cardiac Cl- conductances involves a protein that is phosphorylated by PKA and dephosphorylated by a protein phosphatase, with the dephosphorylating activity being regulated by okadaic acid.
the Cl- conductance of cardiac myocytes is regulated by two different types of phosphorylation sites, and that each site can be dephosphorylated by different protein phosphatases.
phosphorylation of ClC-2 at two different sites is responsible for the incremental activation of the PKA regulated Cl- conductance observed in mammalian ventricular myocytes.
